**A new drive format: files that describe themselves.** Every file now
carries its own key and a sealed label with its real name, and every folder
knows its own name. You can move hidden files around by hand and cloak keeps
track, damaged or overwritten folder lists rebuild themselves, and changing
a password is instant.

> **Drives made by earlier versions don't open in this one.** If you have one
> with anything in it, copy the files out with v0.4.1 first (unlock it and
> copy them to an ordinary folder), then make a new drive, or convert that
> folder, with this version.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.5.0-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.5.0-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again). macFUSE's kernel extension must be
allowed; on Apple Silicon that means its one-time Reduced Security setup.

## New

- **Move hidden files by hand.** With a drive locked, a hidden file or folder
  moved into another of its folders shows up there under its real name.
  Moved into a *different* drive's folder, it waits: that drive's card says
  how many items are waiting, and **More → Bring in files from another
  drive…** lists them, then brings them in with both passwords. It re-seals
  each file's label rather than copying the file, so even large files take a
  moment.
- **Items that go missing are noticed.** If a hidden file or folder is moved
  out of a drive, or deleted, outside cloak, the card says so and **More →
  Show missing items…** lists what went and when. Put one back and it
  reappears.
- **Folder lists repair themselves.** A list that's damaged, or that was
  replaced by copying another folder's contents (with its `manifest.idx`)
  over it, is set aside rather than deleted, and rebuilt from the folder's
  files.
- **Change password…** in a drive's More menu. It's instant: only the drive's
  header changes.

## Safer

- **Each file has its own key**, and its encrypted ends get a fresh seal when
  an edit changes them, so old and new copies of a file (from sync history or
  a backup) don't give each other away.
- **Folder lists, file labels and the drive header are tamper-evident:**
  damage or tampering is reported, never read as garbage.

## Fixed and improved

- **Convert folder:** the button changes to **Convert** after the check, and
  a counter shows progress while converting (and while turning a drive back).
- **Change password and Turn back into a plain folder** could not be closed.
  Fixed.
- **Tab** moves from one password box to the next instead of stopping on the
  show-password button.

## Speed

Reading, writing large files, appending and listing folders run at the same
speed as before. Creating many small files is about 25% slower (each file
now gets its own key and label), and the first edit to the start or end of
an existing file in each editing session takes about 10 ms longer (the fresh
seal).

## Known limitations

- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
